fields.h1: Build a Retail Survey That Compares Every Store
fields.hero_description: Get a retail survey for shoppers and store staff, with every answer tagged by store and saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Behind a Retail Survey
fields.features_subheading: The first three shape what a shopper or associate sees. The last three decide where each answer goes and who hears about it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from one prompt

Describe your stores, who answers, and what each answer should change. Emergent writes the survey and its database from that prompt, and one more sentence edits any question.
fields.feature_2:
A store number on every answer

Each store gets its own QR code and link, so every answer arrives tagged with the store it came from. Compare one location with the rest in a single table, with no sorting by hand.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Shoppers scan the code at the register and answer one question per screen. Associates answer on their own phones during a break, and the survey puts no cap on how many respond.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts to the manager who can fix it

Set a line for any score. When an answer falls under it, the app emails that store's manager or posts in Slack, and the district manager sees the same alert in the app.
fields.feature_5:
Answers in a database you own

Every answer is a row in a database you own, with its store, date, and question. Put this quarter's scores beside last quarter's, or sync the table with your point-of-sale API.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Put the survey on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep a copy there.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a retail survey for my 6 hardware stores that shoppers open from a QR code on the receipt.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a retail survey?

plan.angle: Template sites list generic retail questions and stop at the form. This page treats a retail survey as an operating tool for stores: every answer carries its store number, so a chain sees which location is slipping. It covers the four surveys a store team runs (receipt surveys for shoppers, district manager visit audits, associate pulse checks and requests for items the shelf did not have), each built from a prompt into an app with a database the retailer owns and alerts to the person who acts. Satisfaction scoring theory stays on the customer satisfaction page; after-checkout ecommerce questions stay on the post purchase page.
tab_stories: Wexby Hardware prints a QR code on every receipt that opens a 3-question survey tagged with the store; 1,284 shoppers answer across 6 stores in April, and the Route 9 store rates checkout speed 2.8 of 5, so the regional manager adds a Saturday cashier there.

Sorrelwick Pet Supply's district manager scores each store on a 20-item visit checklist on her phone, and a store under 16 sends its manager an email listing the missed items; the Bayview store scores 14 and its manager gets 6 items.

Kestly Outfitters asks associates 3 anonymous questions every other Friday, and at the Elm Street store agreement with 'I get my schedule 2 weeks ahead' falls from 19 of 24 to 9 of 24 after a May scheduling change.

Fallowby Market asks shoppers at the service desk what they could not find; 312 requests arrive in March, and each Monday the grocery buyer gets a Slack list of the 5 most requested items, led by unsweetened oat milk at 41.
